endpoint.nameHint: Same as the entity name; rename the entity itself to change it
endpoint.descPlaceholder: This is what external callers see
endpoint.paramsEmpty: Agents declare no input parameters: callers send free-form JSON and the agent interprets it

endpoint.tipInternal: Internal only: callable inside this tenant

endpointsTab.definition: An endpoint exposes an agent / workflow as an MCP / RPC entry point for external systems; create one under Agents / Workflows → Endpoints
endpointsTab.helpWhatBody: A call entry point that an agent / workflow exposes to the outside. Calling it over MCP or RPC is the same as calling that agent or workflow.
endpointsTab.helpCreateBody: Open the agent / workflow editor → Endpoints → New endpoint. Each target and protocol can have exactly one endpoint.
endpointsTab.helpCallBody: External systems call {mcp} or {rpc} with the header {auth}. Which endpoints a credential may call is bound under Settings → Service credentials.
endpointsTab.helpCallMore: Each row's Usage has a ready-to-copy connection config and call example.
endpointsTab.helpExposeBody: Exposed = callable from outside the tenant (external credentials, MCP tool registration); internal only = callable inside this tenant, with the endpoint record and config kept. Retracting does not affect in-tenant calls, but once exposed, changes to the target definition immediately affect external callers.
endpointsTab.helpToolBody: Only a workflow's RPC endpoint can be called by other agents as a local tool ({ref}). MCP endpoints are for external systems and never appear in the tool catalog.
endpointsTab.emptyTip: A workflow automatically gets one RPC endpoint (so other flows can call it by name); MCP endpoints are created on demand under Endpoints in the editor. This page only views, exposes / retracts and deletes them.
endpointsTab.exposedLong: Exposed (callable with credentials from outside the tenant)
endpointsTab.deleteManaged: RPC endpoints are managed with their workflow and cannot be deleted separately; disable or deprecate the workflow instead
endpointsTab.deleteBody: Delete endpoint "{name}" ({protocol})? The endpoint marker on the target entity is cleared as well.
endpointsTab.retractConfirm: Retract all endpoints of {name} (turn off Exposed)? Endpoint records and config are kept, and in-tenant calls are unaffected.
endpointsTab.retractedAll: All endpoints of this target are no longer exposed

endpointGuide.title: Endpoint usage
endpointGuide.accessBody: An endpoint has exactly one external address, and it sits on one of two paths depending on the protocol: {mcp} or {rpc}. Every request must carry {auth}; which endpoints a credential may call is decided by the bindings under Settings → Service credentials, and unauthorized endpoints look like they do not exist.
endpointGuide.statusInternal: Internal only (external calls are rejected; turn the switch on in the list first)
endpointGuide.mcpBody: Every exposed MCP endpoint is a standard MCP tool: the tool name equals the endpoint name and its input equals the endpoint's {schema}. Once connected, {list} only lists the endpoints the current credential may access.
endpointGuide.mcpAlertBody: That version has no {init} handshake — every request carries {meta}. Clients defaulting to the older protocol (e.g. 2025-11-25) are rejected at the transport layer, so you need a newer client or a protocol-adapting proxy in front.
endpointGuide.rpcBody: JSON-RPC 2.0: the endpoint name goes into {name} and the business arguments into {args} (the envelope matches MCP's {call}, and {version} defaults to 1). It returns {content} text parts and {isError}; {method} lists the endpoints.
endpointGuide.toolTitle: Use it as an agent tool
endpointGuide.toolBodyRef: A workflow's RPC endpoint shows up as {ref} in the tool grant catalog; once granted, the model can call it directly. Path: agent editor → Tool grants (for skills, tick them under Tool dependencies).
endpointGuide.toolBodyUnavailable: Only a workflow's RPC endpoint enters the tool grant system ({reason}). This endpoint takes part in no grants and can only be called from outside at the address above.
endpointGuide.toolBodyGeneric: Only a workflow's RPC endpoint enters the tool grant system, as {ref}, tickable under the agent editor → Tool grants. MCP and agent endpoints are for external systems only and never appear in the tool catalog.
endpointGuide.reasonMcp: MCP endpoints are for external systems only
endpointGuide.reasonAgent: agent endpoints never enter the tool catalog; agent-to-agent calls go through call_agent
endpointGuide.noteInternal: An internal-only endpoint cannot be called from outside: MCP does not register the tool and RPC answers "endpoint is not exposed". The switch in the list is exactly expose / retract.
endpointGuide.noteOnePerTarget: Each target and protocol can have exactly one endpoint; changing the input schema immediately affects callers (the tool contract changed).
endpointGuide.noteDecoupled: The endpoint name is decoupled from the target entity name: renaming the workflow does not rename the endpoint, and vice versa.
endpointGuide.noteCredScope: Credential scope is decided per target entity: all protocol endpoints of the same agent share one grant.
